The pack frame is kept in `derivedFrom` because provenance is worth more than the wrong pointer. **Drawn 31 August** — `FnB Board 3.dc.html` frame `fnb-3h`. **Matched on frame title against screen name, constrained to this board’s platforms.** These packs label by board position (`GM-6C`) rather than naming the screen, so the title is the only join — *Exceptions, Re-Fire & Unavailable Items* matched at 1.0. **A cross-platform title match was refused**: `Outlet Management` scored 0.85 against a partner-portal screen, which is how a mapping goes wrong quietly.
densityReason: **Bumped by somebody with flour on their hands, read from two metres, in a room where nobody is sitting down.** A kitchen display is not a back office at a different width.
patternReason: `list86Events` reads the population and `getHaccpStatus` reads one of them — list, select, act
purpose: Exceptions, Re-Fire & Unavailable Items — board 3 of the client F&B design set.

gaps.why: **2 declared operations reach no component on this screen**: getHaccpStatus, list86Events. Either the screen is missing what calls them, or the declaration is residue.

components.notes: **One ticket per card, ordered by promise time not arrival.** A ticket due in two minutes sits above one that arrived first, because a kitchen works to when food is wanted.
Depth, oldest ticket age, station load. **Three numbers, glanceable** — anything a chef has to read is a number they will not read.

states.loading: The rail, oldest ticket first. **The count renders before the tickets** — a kitchen wants to know how deep it is before it reads anything.
states.error: Could not reach the platform. **The rail is still live from cache** and every bump is queued.
states.emptyFirstRun: **No tickets. The kitchen is clear**, and that is worth saying plainly rather than showing a blank rail — a screen that looks broken and a screen that means nothing to do are the same picture otherwise.
states.emptyNoResults: Nothing matches this station or course filter. **The rail is not empty** — the filter is narrow, and on a kitchen screen that distinction is the difference between calm and panic.
states.emptyNoAccess: This display is not assigned to a station. **Assignment is a back-office act** — a kitchen screen does not choose what it shows.
states.offline: **Amber, and it keeps working.** The kitchen still has to send food out — a display that blanks mid-service is worse than one that says it is behind, and every bump journals locally and syncs when the network returns.
